newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to ask details about loan plan for Kirch.
newsitem.headline: EU to ask details about loan plan for Kirch.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to ask the German authorities shortly to provide information about a loan plan for Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch.

"We will undoubtedly send a letter to the Bonn authorities, as we always do in similar cases, requesting an explanation," a Commission official said on Tuesday. The official said the letter would be sent by the Commission's competition services.
Kirch has been offered a loan which could be as big as one billion marks and would be sponsored by the German state of Bavaria.

Landesanstalt fuer Aufbaufinanzierung (LfA), the state-controlled bank, alone is to contribute with several hundred million marks. But it has said that several commercial banks are involved and the loan would be granted at market conditions.

The Commission must examine all loans which may involve state subsidies. Kirch competitors, including German pay-television channel Premiere, have publicly voiced concern about the plan. Premiere is controlled by Bertelsmann and Canal Plus.
The loan is meant to help Kirch overcome financial problems linked with the launch of its digital television station DF1. -- Amelia Torres 322 2876841
